topics.description: A Korean dynasty that ruled from 918 to 1392 and became subject to Mongol influence during the reign of Kublai Khan.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This region’s rule by Empress Min in the late 19th century led a Western scholar to call it a “hermit kingdom.” In 1598, the Ming Dynasty helped defend this region against an invading fleet at the Battle of Noryang. In the thirteenth century, this region’s (*) Goryeo Dynasty fell to Kublai Khan, and its Joseon dynasty ended in 1897 with its invasion by Japan. For ten points, name this East Asian peninsula that is, today, split into two countries.
parts.answer: Korea (accept Korean Peninsula; accept Koryo until “Goryeo” is read; accept North and South Korea only after “today” is read)

topics.description: A war from 395 to 387 BCE in which Athens, Corinth, Thebes, and Argos opposed Sparta before the King's Peace ended the conflict.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The King's Peace ended a war named for this city that broke out shortly after the Peloponnesian (pel-uh-puh-NEE-zhun) War, which itself followed a dispute between this city and Athens over the colony of Corcyra (kor-SEER-uh). During the spring of the years before and after each Olympic Games, this city hosted the (*) Isthmian (IZTH-mee-un) Games. This city, legendarily founded by Sisyphus (SIS-if-us), names one of the original three Greek orders of columns along with Ionic and Doric. For 10 points, what ancient Greek city's Christian community received two letters from Paul in the New Testament?
parts.answer: Corinth [or Corinthian War; or Corinthian order; or First or Second Corinthians]

topics.description: The lower rural social class in German-speaking lands that rebelled during the 1525 German Peasants' War and issued the Twelve Articles.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These people promulgated the Twelve Articles under the leadership of Thomas Muntzer. Martin Luther compared these people to “mad dogs” in a tract titled “Against the Thieving, Murderous Hordes of [these people].” These people carried out a 1525 (*) revolt in Germany, and were likened to the working-class proletariat in an analysis by Friedrich Engels. For 10 points, name this lower class of people in Medieval society.

topics.description: The Norman duke who defeated Harold Godwinson at the Battle of Hastings and conquered England in 1066.

parts.label: L
parts.question: George R. R. Martin is well-versed in medieval history. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: The Lannisters and Starks were based on the Lancasters and Yorks, who waged the Wars of the Roses in this  country.
parts.answer: England [or Great Britain; or the United Kingdom]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Aegon the Conqueror’s conquest of Westeros after landing at King’s Landing mirrors this Norman duke’s  conquest of England. This leader won the Battle of Hastings.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Martin borrowed elements of his bloody Red Wedding scene from this country’s “Black Dinner.” This country  allied with France in the Auld Alliance.

topics.description: The 48 BCE battle in which Julius Caesar decisively defeated the forces of Pompey the Great during the Roman Civil War.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man won the Battle of Pharsalus against the forces of Pompey the Great, securing victory in a civil war. This man captured the chief Vercingetorix at the end of the Gallic Wars, which he won. This man brought his army across the (*) Rubicon in defiance of the Senate, but was eventually assassinated on the Ides of March. For 10 points, name this Roman dictator who was stabbed by Brutus.

topics.description: Pedro was the regnal name shared by Pedro I and Pedro II, the first two emperors of independent Brazil.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Saraiva-Cotegipe Law and the Rio Branco Law began this process in one country. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this process completed by the Golden Law in that country. The U.S. completed this process by passing the 13th Amendment. A description is acceptable.
parts.answer: abolishing slavery [or ending slavery; prompt on abolition with “what was abolished?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Golden Law was passed in this largest South American country, the only one with Portuguese as its official language.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Golden Law was passed by a monarch with this name. Two monarchs with this name ruled Brazil immediately after its independence from Portugal.
parts.answer: Pedro [accept Dom Pedro I or Dom Pedro II]

topics.description: A Turkic ethnic group of Central Asia whose historical kingdoms included the Uyghur Khaganate and whose modern homeland is the Xinjiang region of China.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These people’s namesake Khaganate was destroyed in 840 after an invasion by the Kirghiz. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these people whose Khaganate had its capital at Ordu-Baliq. These people later went on to be the dominant ethnic group in the Tarim Basin following the Dzungar Genocide.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Uighurs converted from Buddhism to this religion over the course of several centuries. After converting to this religion, many Uighur kingdoms came to rely on the Qur’an for legal purposes.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Some Uighurs joined the Dzungars in their conflicts with this dynasty. The Dzungar Khanate was destroyed as part of this dynasty’s Ten Great Campaigns, waged during the reign of this dynasty’s Qianlong Emperor.

topics.topic: Great Stand on the Ugra River
topics.description: The Great Stand on the Ugra River was the 1480 standoff that marked the effective end of Tatar domination over the Grand Duchy of Moscow.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A monarch from this city initiated a process of “gathering lands” under its rule using highinterest loans and thus became known as “Kalitá” (KAH-lit-AH) or “moneybags.” A “Grand  Prince” from this city reclaimed autonomy from the Tatars at the Great Stand on the (*) Ugra  River. That prince of this city married the former Byzantine princess Zoe Palaiologina (PAIL-ee-ohLOWG-ee-nah) and promoted the idea of this city as “the third Rome.” A form of the word “Caesar”  began to be used in 1547 by the grand princes of this city. For 10 points, name this city where Ivan IV  (ee-VAN the fourth) proclaimed himself “tsar.”
parts.answer: Moscow [or Grand Duchy of Moscow; do not accept or prompt on “Muscovy”]

topics.description: An intelligence-sharing alliance comprising the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The French government recalled its ambassadors to the United States and this country in response to a 2021 nuclear submarine deal which replaced an existing deal with France. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country. Joe Biden and this country’s prime minister, Scott Morrison, announced that the U.S. would sell nuclear submarines to this country.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This near neighbor of Australia won’t allow its nuclear submarines into its territorial waters, in keeping with its “Nuclear Free Zone” policy. The Rainbow Warrior was sunk by French agents in this country’s city of Auckland.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The United States, New Zealand, and Australia are three of the countries in this intelligence alliance of English-speaking countries. This intelligence alliance uses the Stone Ghost network to share information.

topics.description: The era of political fragmentation in China following the decline of the Han Dynasty, conventionally dated from 220 to 280 CE.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This dynasty was briefly interrupted by Wang Mang’s Xin Dynasty. The Records of the Grand Historian was written during this dynasty, which was founded by Liu Bang after the fall of the Qin Dynasty. This dynasty was weakened by the (*) Yellow Turban Rebellion, leading to the tumultuous Three Kingdoms Period. For 10 points, what Chinese dynasty shares its name with China’s majority ethnic group?
